QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_49

question.text: A company with a face value of Rs.10 per share declares a 40% dividend. If the current market price of the share is Rs.200, what is the dividend yield?

explanation.text: The Logic: Step 1: Dividend per share = 40% of face value = 40% x Rs.10 = Rs.4. Step 2: Dividend yield = Dividend per share / Market price per share = Rs.4 / Rs.200 = 0.02 = 2%. The dividend declared is a percentage of face value, but dividend yield is calculated on market price. The Trap: 40% (option B) is the dividend rate on face value, NOT the dividend yield on market price. This is the classic trap -- confusing dividend rate with dividend yield. 20% (option C) and 5% (option D) result from incorrect calculations. Note: This exact example (Rs.10 face value, 40% dividend, Rs.200 market price) is from the NISM XII workbook.
